Infirmier(ère) auxiliaire – Médecine / Courte durée à Chibougamau | Baie-James
 Services SFT est une agence de placement de premier plan spécialisée dans le déploiement de professionnels de la santé partout au Québec. Nous accompagnons les établissements du réseau public dans la couverture de leurs besoins en main-d'œuvre indépendante, tout en offrant à nos candidats des opportunités de carrière uniques, stables et hautement valorisées.
 Nous recherchons actuellement une Infirmière auxiliaire ou un Infirmier auxiliaire pour combler un mandat de longue durée en soins aigus.
 Description du poste
 Joignez-vous à l'équipe de la Direction des soins infirmiers (DSI) au Centre de santé de Chibougamau . Intégré(e) au département de Médecine / Courte durée , vous assurerez la prise en charge, le suivi clinique et la dispensation des soins de santé auprès de patients hospitalisés en phase active.
 Détails du mandat : 
 Période du besoin : Du 11 novembre 2026 au 14 mars 2027 (Mandat de 4 mois).
 Quarts de travail : Flexibilité requise sur les quarts de Jour, Soir et Nuit .
 Type d'horaire : Horaires flexibles de 8 heures, 12 heures ou 16 heures selon les besoins de l'établissement.
 Temps de repas : 45 minutes pour les quarts de 8 heures | 1h40 pour les quarts de 12 heures.
 Horaire atypique : Non.
 Garde (On-Call) : Non.
 Orientation : Une période d'orientation est requise et entièrement planifiée à votre arrivée.
 Vos responsabilités
 Collaborer avec l'équipe multidisciplinaire pour offrir des soins infirmiers de qualité aux patients de l'unité de médecine et courte durée.
 Évaluer l'état de santé des patients, surveiller les signes vitaux et déceler les changements cliniques.
 Participer activement à la surveillance cardiologique (arythmie) et à l'administration sécuritaire de la médication selon votre champ de pratique.
 Assurer la tenue rigoureuse des dossiers cliniques et participer aux transmissions inter-quarts.
 Profil recherché
 Ordre professionnel : Membre en règle et inscription valide au tableau de l' Ordre des infirmières et infirmiers auxiliaires du Québec (OIIAQ) .
 Expérience exigée : Minimum de 2 ans d'expérience consolidée en médecine active .
 Formations spécifiques : Avoir complété avec succès le cours d'arythmie ( Strictement obligatoire ).
 Exigences logistiques : Aucun permis de conduire ni véhicule automobile n'est requis pour ce mandat.
 Aptitudes : Rigueur professionnelle, grande capacité d’adaptation aux horaires variables, esprit d'équipe et excellente gestion du stress en milieu de courte durée.
 Avantages:
 Un accompagnement personnalisé par l'équipe des Normes SFT durant toute la durée de votre assignation.
 Un mandat de longue durée offrant une excellente stabilité professionnelle pour la saison hivernale.
 Une rémunération très compétitive selon les barèmes de main-d'œuvre indépendante de Services SFT.
 Taux horaire 45$/H et 50$/jour travaillé.
 Intéressé(e) ? 
 Envoyez votre CV à jour à :
 info.sft@sftechniques.com 
 Vous pouvez également nous contacter au (438) 946-6340 .
 Notre équipe se fera un plaisir de répondre à toutes vos questions.

Richmond, BC | Full-Time, Permanent | On-Site 
 Keep The Operations Moving, From Dock to Delivery 
 The best manufacturing teams run on accuracy, accountability, and people who take pride in getting things right.
 Our client is looking for a detail-oriented, hands-on team member who enjoys keeping materials organized, orders accurate, and production running smoothly.
 If you like work where you can see the results of your effort, enjoy being part of a team, and want to build a career in manufacturing and operations, this is a great opportunity.
 This is not a single-task warehouse role. It’s a cross-trained position supporting both warehouse and production, where quality, safety, and problem-solving matter as much as speed.
 Why This Role Matters 
 In a manufacturing environment, the right material in the right place at the right time makes the difference between smooth production and costly delays.
 This role exists to make sure that happens. By keeping inventory accurate, materials available, and shipments correct and on time, you’ll directly support their ability to deliver high-quality equipment to customers around the world.
 About Our Client 
 They design and manufacture high-performance mixers and agitators for industrial process applications worldwide. Their customers operate in energy, chemicals, water treatment, mining, and natural resources.
 Their strength goes beyond the equipment itself. They focus on understanding our customers’ processes and delivering engineered solutions that improve operational performance and create measurable value.
 As they continue to grow, they’re investing in the systems, processes, and people needed to strengthen their market presence. They’re looking for team members who are careful, collaborative, and committed to doing things the right way.
 What You’ll Own 
 You’ll receive, inspect, and verify incoming materials, making sure quantities, documentation, and quality meet company requirements.
 You’ll store and organize inventory so the warehouse runs efficiently and production always has what it needs.
 You’ll pick, stage, kit, and issue materials for manufacturing, assembly, and customer orders.
 You’ll prepare, package, verify, and load outbound shipments, ensuring accuracy and compliance with packaging requirements.
 You’ll perform receiving and pre-shipment quality checks and flag damaged or non-conforming materials.
 You’ll work with the Production Coordinator and Supply Chain Specialist to resolve material, inventory, and shipment issues.
 You’ll assist with annual inventory audits and support continuous improvement initiatives.
 You’ll pitch in on assembly and other operational activities as needed.
 Most importantly, you’ll help maintain a clean, organized, and safe working environment by following safety procedures and reporting hazards.
 What Success Looks Like 
 Success in this role is measured by accuracy, reliability, and teamwork.
 You’ll know you’re succeeding when:
 Inventory records match what’s on the shelf
 Production has the materials it needs, when it needs them
 Incoming and outgoing orders are accurate, complete, and on time
 Damaged or non-conforming materials are caught and communicated early
 Colleagues across operations rely on you for clear communication and follow-through
 Safety and quality are part of everything you do
 What Makes You Successful 
 You’ll thrive in this role if you enjoy hands-on work and take pride in getting the details right.
 You’re organized, you notice when something doesn’t look right, and you follow through on your commitments. You work well independently and as part of a team, and you’re comfortable reading and interpreting purchase orders, packing slips, work orders, and shipping documents.
 You’ll be especially successful if you bring experience in receiving, warehousing, inventory control, shipping, manufacturing, or production support. Experience with ERP, inventory management, or warehouse management systems is an asset.
 Qualifications 
 High school diploma or equivalent
 1–3 years of experience in receiving, warehousing, inventory control, shipping, manufacturing, or production support preferred
 Strong attention to detail and accuracy
 Ability to read and interpret purchase orders, packing slips, work orders, and shipping documentation
 Strong organizational, problem-solving, and time-management skills
 Basic computer proficiency and data entry skills
 Experience with ERP, inventory, or warehouse management systems (asset)
 Forklift certification or willingness to obtain it (asset)
 Commitment to safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement
 Physical requirements: The ability to lift, move, and handle materials safely; to stand, walk, bend, and reach throughout the workday; and to work in a warehouse and manufacturing environment, safely operating material handling equipment when authorized.
 What’s In It F or You
 Full-time, permanent position (40 hours per week)
 Practical, hands-on training and development
 Cross-training across both warehouse and production functions
 Exposure to engineered industrial equipment used across diverse industries
 Opportunities for professional growth and career advancement
 A collaborative team environment that values initiative and problem-solving
 Meaningful work that directly supports customer success
 Ready to Keep Things Moving? 
 If you take pride in accuracy, safety, and teamwork, and want to be part of a growing manufacturer, we’d love to hear from you.
 Apply with your resume and tell us about your experience in receiving, warehousing, inventory, shipping, or production support, and anything you’d like us to know about your commitment to safety and quality.

Senior Geotechnical Engineer | Tailings & Mine Waste | P.Eng
 We are seeking an accomplished Senior Geotechnical Engineer – Tailings & Mine Waste to join our growing Tailings & Mine Waste team .  Our team delivers engineering and consulting services for tailings storage facilities, mine-waste facilities, waste rock facilities, and related mining infrastructure, supporting clients through investigation, design, construction, operation, monitoring, and closure. This is an opportunity to contribute to complex projects while working alongside experienced engineers and multidisciplinary teams.
 Why Join Equilibrium? 
 Global reach. Specialist expertise. Real influence. 
 Equilibrium brings together the global reach and expertise of an established consultancy with the autonomy and agility of a specialist firm.
 Here, you’ll work closely with experienced leaders, have a genuine voice in the business and see the impact of your work firsthand. As we grow, you’ll have the opportunity to take ownership, deepen your expertise in geotechnical engineering and mine waste, and play a meaningful role in shaping what comes next.
 We want our people to grow with the business, build meaningful relationships and make a lasting contribution - not simply be part of the team, but help build the future of Equilibrium.
 The Role: 
 As a Senior Geotechnical Engineer, Tailings & Mine Waste , you’ll deliver complex tailings and mine waste projects, provide technical guidance, and work closely with clients and multidisciplinary teams. You’ll have the opportunity to apply your technical expertise across investigations, design, and facility assessments, mentor developing engineers, and contribute to the continued growth of Equilibrium’s Mine Waste practice.
 You will:
 Deliver Technical Projects: Manage geotechnical investigations, assessments, and designs for tailings, waste rock spoils and other mine waste facilities, confirming safe work practices, schedule, budget, and client requirements are met.
 Perform Technical Analysis: Perform, oversee, and review geotechnical analyses, interpret field and monitoring data, develop geotechnical models, and provide practical, risk-informed engineering recommendations.
 Support Field Activities: Plan and coordinate geotechnical investigations, inspections, and construction support activities, providing safety oversight, technical direction and responding to site conditions and emerging project requirements.
 Provide Technical Review: Prepare and review engineering reports, calculations, specifications, and technical documentation, while supporting technical reviews, dam safety assessments, risk evaluations, and quality assurance and quality control.
 Support Clients & Project Delivery: Serve as a point of contact for assigned scopes, communicate project status, technical findings and recommendations, and contribute to project planning, proposals, schedules, budgets, and client meetings.
 Develop People: Provide technical guidance, mentorship, and review to junior engineers, engineers-in-training, technologists, and field staff, supporting their professional development.
 Drive Technical Excellence: Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and contribute to continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, industry best practices, and the development of tools, workflows, and quality practices within the Mine Waste practice.
 What We’re Looking For: 
 7 - 10 years of relevant experience in geotechnical engineering, mining, engineering consulting, mine waste, tailings, or project delivery.
 Demonstrated experience in geotechnical design and evaluation of tailings dams, waste rock spoils, and/or co-management structures.
 Demonstrated commitment to health and safety, with experience identifying and managing risks in mine site, field, and project environments. Dam Safety experience considered an asset.
 Strong technical judgement, leadership and project coordination skills.
 Strong interpersonal and emotional intelligence, with the ability to communicate thoughtfully, build trust, provide constructive technical feedback, and navigate challenging situations with empathy.
 Experience contributing to business development, cross-selling, and building long-term client relationships.
 Willingness to travel to mine sites as required.
 Education & Certifications: 
 Bachelor’s degree or higher in Engineering (Civil, Geotechnical, Geological, or related discipline).
 Professional Engineering designation (P.Eng.) or equivalent professional registration required where applicable.
 About Equilibrium: 
 Complex challenges. Practical solutions. Technical excellence. 
 Equilibrium is a specialist technical consultancy serving the global mining and natural resources sectors. We bring together expertise in geotechnical engineering, structural geology, and hydrogeology, to solve complex technical challenges and deliver practical solutions for our clients.
 Founded by internationally respected technical leaders, we combine deep technical expertise with a practical, solutions-focused approach and close client relationships. Our multidisciplinary teams work across regions and disciplines to deliver work that is technically sound, practical and fit for purpose.
 Technical excellence is at the heart of what we do. We are committed to continuously improving our expertise, how we work and the value we deliver to our clients.
 Our People & Culture: 
 Different perspectives make us stronger. 
 We believe bringing together different experiences and ways of thinking makes our teams stronger and our work better. More than half of our team are women, reflecting the inclusive and collaborative culture we are building at Equilibrium.
 We look for people who are technically excellent, curious, empathetic and generous with their knowledge. Initiative, collaboration and fresh thinking shape how we work, while respect and transparency guide how we work with one another.
 We want people to feel heard, supported and empowered to contribute — whether that's sharing an idea, challenging an assumption or helping a colleague succeed.
 Our values — excellence, transparency, diversity and mindfulness of our impact — guide how we work with each other, serve our clients and contribute to our communities and the planet. 
 Compensation: 
 We expect that the salary package to be in the below range depending on experience, qualifications, and skills. The final compensation package will be determined based on the successful candidate’s background and fit for the role.
 $120,000 to $145,000 CAD per year + Benefits + Bonus
 Location: 
 Equilibrium operates globally, with offices in South Brisbane, Australia; Vancouver, Canada; and Portland and Phoenix, USA. 
 We are primarily accepting applications from candidates from within Canada.  Flexible hybrid and remote-based arrangements will be considered for the right individual, depending on location and project requirements. 
 Additional Requirements: 
 Must be legally authorized to work in the country where the position is based. 
 Periodic domestic and/or international travel may be required for project assignments, meetings, training, client engagements, field investigations, and other business purposes, including travel to remote project and mine sites.
 As the Employer operates globally, flexibility in work schedule may be required to support collaboration across different time zones.
 Depending on project or client requirements, the role may require security, background, criminal record, drug and alcohol, or other screening.

 Posting Information:
 This posting is for an existing vacancy.

 Job Description: 
 Primary Purpose 
 Reporting to the Executive Director, Facilities, the Director, Energy & Mechanical Operations provides leadership and operational oversight for the University of Waterloo’s Mechanical, Electrical and HVAC and Controls building infrastructure teams to ensure safe and reliable day to day operations. In addition, this role is also responsible for the universities energy management programs and storm water management systems across the campus.  This includes ensuring the safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of campus utilities while advancing energy conservation initiatives that support the University’s sustainability goals.
 The Director leads the planning and management of utility infrastructure operations, supports long-term renewal planning for energy systems, and works collaboratively across Facilities and campus partners to optimize energy performance and system reliability.
 University of Waterloo infrastructure supports more than eight million square feet of academic, research, and administrative space across multiple campuses. The associated energy systems are critical to maintaining safe and effective teaching, research, and campus operations. The Director works in close partnership with the Chief Stationary Engineer to ensure that energy and utility systems are planned, resourced, and operated in alignment with institutional priorities, regulatory requirements, and long‑term infrastructure strategies.
 This role contributes to the Plant Operations goal of providing a safe, reliable, accessible, and well-maintained campus environment through service excellence, operational efficiency, and responsible stewardship of energy resources.
 Key Accountabilities 
 Strategic Planning 
 Acts as the subject matter expert and ensures implementation of the Deferred Capital Renewal plan for energy utility and building systems, ensuring alignment with the University’s long-term academic, research, and campus growth objectives.
 Establishes long-term strategies for the capacity, reliability, and resilience of campus energy infrastructure, including district energy systems, electrical distribution, and utility supply.
 Identifies and prioritizes infrastructure renewal and modernization initiatives related to energy and core building systems to mitigate risks associated with aging infrastructure and deferred maintenance.
 Provides strategic advice to the Executive Director, Facilities and senior leadership regarding long-term utility infrastructure requirements, emerging technologies, and infrastructure risks.
 Directs the development of long-range infrastructure investment plans, balancing operational needs, sustainability commitments, and available funding.
 Develops performance indicators and analytical frameworks to support data-driven decision-making related to infrastructure performance, asset lifecycle management, and system reliability.
 Monitors external trends including energy markets, regulatory changes, and technological advancements and assesses their potential impact on campus infrastructure planning.
 Works collaboratively with the Chief Stationary Engineer to align utility and energy infrastructure planning, performance objectives, and renewal priorities within Central Plants operating capabilities and constraints.
 Partners with the Chief Stationary Engineer to assess operational risks, system reliability trends, and capacity limitations, and to develop mitigation and investment strategies.
 Energy Management 
 Leads the University of Waterloo’s Energy Management program, identifying and implementing initiatives to improve energy efficiency and reduce institutional energy consumption.
 Works collaboratively with the Sustainability Office and campus partners to support the University’s sustainability goals.
 Provides technical expertise to the Executive Director, Facilities on matters related to energy consumption, utility supply, sustainability initiatives, and energy efficiency opportunities.
 Oversees development of multi-year utility forecasts, incorporating projected consumption, regulatory changes, and energy market conditions.
 Directs the evaluation of campus energy systems to identify energy conservation opportunities and operational improvements.
 Oversees the development of business cases, funding proposals, and external submissions related to energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives.
 Provides oversight to the Energy Manager in the negotiation and management of utility supply contracts and agreements.
 Collaborates with faculty, staff, and students on the implementation of energy reduction initiatives, ensuring alignment with the University’s academic and research mission.
 Infrastructure Renewal 
 Contributes to capital planning and infrastructure renewal planning related to energy, utility and building systems.
 Provides technical input into the prioritization of deferred maintenance and system renewal initiatives affecting campus energy infrastructure.
 Supports development of business cases and capital funding requests for infrastructure renewal and modernization projects.
 Collaborates with the Design and Construction team to ensure projects involving utility infrastructure are effectively coordinated.
 Works with campus partners to identify opportunities to improve energy performance, operational efficiency, and infrastructure resiliency.
 Project Management and Procurement 
 Provides oversight to staff managing energy and utility infrastructure projects, including system upgrades and efficiency initiatives.
 Ensures projects are delivered in accordance with University procurement policies, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
 Supports project planning and implementation while ensuring adherence to health and safety standards and construction regulations.

About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





Why we're looking for you



At Owner, authentication and authorization sit at the center of trust. Every restaurant owner, employee, partner, and internal teammate depends on secure, reliable access to the right tools at the right time — whether they’re ringing up orders, balancing the books, or supporting customers behind the scenes.



We’re building the next generation of our identity and access platform, and we need an exceptional engineer to help us get there. You’ll join a small, high-trust team with direct ownership over login, session management, permissions, roles, service-to-service auth, and the APIs and infrastructure every product team at Owner builds on top of. This is a rare opportunity to shape a foundational security platform at a fast-growing company — one that has to scale with our product surface, our customer base, and the complexity of the restaurants we serve.



This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States or Canada.



The impact you'll have



 - Help build the foundation for secure access at Owner — design and improve the authentication and authorization systems that power every product surface across the platform.

 - Own critical auth infrastructure end to end — contribute to systems for login, sessions, token management, service-to-service auth, account security, and access enforcement.

 - Improve reliability and observability — instrument auth services with the alerting, dashboards, and runbooks needed to detect issues quickly and keep critical access flows healthy.

 - Raise the security bar — identify risks, improve controls, and help ensure authentication and authorization are designed thoughtfully from the beginning, not added as an afterthought.

 - Leverage AI tools to move faster — use AI tooling to accelerate your work, from writing and reviewing code to exploring solutions and automating repetitive tasks.

 - Help us build a great team — interview candidates, share technical context, and raise the bar for how we build.



Who you’ll work with



 - A small, focused authentication and authorization team — you’ll work closely with a tight-knit group of engineers who own identity and access end to end.

 - Engineers across product, platform, infrastructure, and security — auth is a foundation every team depends on, so you’ll partner closely on APIs, access patterns, and implementation standards.

 - Product and Design — to ensure access flows are secure, intuitive, and aligned with the needs of restaurants and internal teams.



Minimum requirements



 - 8+ years of experience building and shipping production backend systems, with a track record of owning critical services end to end — not just contributing to them.

 - Comfort with Typescript or Javascript — with deep experience in building web-scale applications.

 - Hands-on experience building authentication, authorization, identity, permissions, security, or similar platform infrastructure.

 - Strong understanding of API design, distributed systems, databases, and operational reliability.

 - Strong sense of ownership and urgency — you don’t wait for perfect requirements, you drive toward clarity and keep things moving.



Compensation and benefits

 

 - The estimated starting base salary range for this role is $230K-$250K depending on level, location and experience, plus a generous pre-IPO equity package

 - Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, work from anywhere (remote-first workplace), unlimited PTO - plus extra fun perks!





Notice - Employment Scams

Communication from our team regarding job opportunities will only be made by an Owner team member with an @owner.com email address.



We do not conduct interviews over email or chat platforms, and we will never ask you to provide personal or financial information such as your mailing address, social security number, credit card numbers or banking information. If you believe you are being contacted by a scammer, please mark the communication as "phishing" or “spam” and do not respond.

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We're looking for an Intermediate Software Engineer to be part of our Software Engineering team.

You could join one of the following teams:

Trust Engineering: Trust Engineering helps keep our Service Providers and our platform safe. We are responsible for providing layered protection at the infra and application level by integrating protections from a variety of third-party security/risk/authentication providers and building our own custom risk/threat logic. We also build tooling and experiences for our frontline security operations teams to improve their ability to mitigate security incidents and build robust controls to prevent future occurrences.

Harbour Foundations: The Harbour Foundations team is building the internal foundation for an AI-powered customer journey at Jobber. Reporting to the Manager, Software Engineering, the Intermediate Software Engineer will collaborate with other Software Development members on a Scrum team to build an industry-leading product that helps our customers and their small businesses be successful. We’re looking for people who are ready to solve problems that millions of entrepreneurs are facing and who are eager to develop their craft while contributing to the team’s success.

In this role, you must be committed to writing well-tested, scalable, and well-organized code. In addition, you will customize, extend and experiment with tools, models, harnesses and processes to increase your effectiveness. You’ll have opportunities to learn, collaborate, and grow while supporting your team in delivering high-quality solutions.



As an Intermediate Software Engineer, you will:

 - Contribute to the design, development, and delivery of features that address customer needs, collaborating with cross-functional teams

 - Work closely with senior engineers to refine requirements and scope technical solutions.

 - Write, review, and maintain clean, scalable, and well-documented code.

 - Participate in code reviews to ensure code quality and maintainability.

 - Collaborate with your team to identify and solve technical challenges.

 - Share knowledge and learn from others through paired programming, team discussions, and technical documentation.

 - Stay curious and keep up to date with the latest tools, technologies, and best practices in software development.

 - Build with AI as a core part of how you work. We expect engineers to delegate real work to agents daily, verify what comes back, and keep improving their own setup so each task makes the next one easier.

To be successful, you should have:

 - Proficiency in writing clean, maintainable, and testable code.

 - Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development methodologies.

 - A structured understanding of common backend frameworks, technologies, and patterns.

 - Familiarity working with observability tools such as DataDog.

 - Strong problem-solving skills and a collaborative mindset.

 - A willingness to learn, adapt, and grow as part of a team.

 - Daily hands-on experience building with agentic AI tools, beyond autocomplete or chat: you delegate real work to agents as part of how you ship.

It would be great (but not a deal-breaker) if you had:

 - Experience with our development stack: React, React Native, TypeScript, Ruby on Rails 

 - Familiarity with GraphQL API Layer and its optimization.

 - Prior experience working on scalable distributed systems.

 - Exposure to background processing frameworks (e.g., Sidekiq, Active Jobs).

 Êtes-vous prêt(e) à faire évoluer votre carrière tout en contribuant à apporter des changements positifs sur les marchés émergents ? 
 Nous recherchons un(e) Associé(e) principal(e), Impact ou d’un(e) agent(e), Climat et impact !   
 Rejoignez FinDev Canada, l’institution financière de développement du Canada ! Nous travaillons avec et par l’intermédiaire du secteur privé pour faire progresser l’action en faveur du climat et de la nature, l’égalité des genres et le développement des marchés dans les économies en développement. Rejoindre FinDev Canada, c’est intégrer une organisation en pleine croissance et animée par une mission, où votre expertise contribue directement à un impact significatif et mesurable à travers le monde. 
 Type de contrat : Permanent
 Lieu : Le siège social de FinDev Canada est situé au centre-ville de Montréal. Pour le candidat idéal, Ottawa ou Toronto seront pris en considération, avec la possibilité de travailler selon un modèle hybride, l’exigence actuelle étant de trois jours de présence au bureau par semaine (sous réserve de modifications).  
 Détails de la rémunération 
 Niveau 16 : Le salaire se situe généralement entre 74 297 $ et 99 063 $ par année, selon les qualifications et l’expérience, auquel s’ajoute une rémunération incitative liée au rendement. 
 Niveau 17 : Le salaire se situe généralement entre 84 698 $ et 112 931 $ par année, selon les qualifications et l’expérience, auquel s’ajoute une rémunération incitative liée au rendement. 
 Pourquoi vous aimerez travailler chez nous 
 Un travail qui fait la différence : nous sommes animés par notre mission de promouvoir une croissance durable et inclusive sur les marchés émergents et dans les économies en développement. Chaque poste contribue à créer un impact positif et durable – pour nos clients, les marchés que nous desservons et les communautés du monde entier.  
 Des collègues inspirants : Rejoignez une équipe diversifiée et talentueuse venue du monde entier, qui apporte une richesse d’expérience, de connaissances et de passion à tout ce que nous faisons. Nous sommes convaincus que les résultats solides découlent de partenariats solides : travailler ensemble, partager nos points de vue et instaurer la confiance pour atteindre des objectifs communs.  
 Nos valeurs fondamentales : Notre culture repose sur la collaboration, l’agilité, l’impact et le respect. Nous travaillons ensemble au sein d’équipes diversifiées, nous accueillons le changement et l’innovation, et nous restons concentrés sur la création d’un impact significatif et durable, tout en nous traitant les uns les autres avec intégrité, empathie et respect.  
 Avantages et bénéfices : Notre offre de rémunération globale va bien au-delà du simple salaire. Nous proposons un ensemble complet d’avantages conçu pour répondre aux besoins variés et aux différentes étapes de la vie de nos collaborateurs.  
 Présentation de l’équipe 
 L’équipe de l’Impact du développement est responsable de l’évaluation, de la mesure et du suivi des retombées sur le développement des investissements et activités de financement de FinDev Canada tout au long du cycle d’investissement. Grâce à des pratiques rigoureuses de gestion et de mesure de l’impact, l’équipe veille à ce que nos opérations contribuent de façon significative à l’action climatique et à la préservation de la nature, à l’égalité des genres et au développement des marchés. 
 Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) associé(e) principal(e) ou d’un(e) agent(e), Climat et impact afin de soutenir et de diriger les évaluations d’impact liées aux occasions d’investissement et de financement dans les secteurs prioritaires de FinDev Canada. Relevant du directeur ou de la directrice, Impact du développement, la personne retenue travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les équipes d’investissement et les parties prenantes internes afin de mettre en œuvre l’approche d’impact de FinDev Canada tout en contribuant à l’évolution continue de nos pratiques de mesure et de gestion de l’impact.
 Vos missions 
 Effectuer le présélectionnement, la diligence raisonnable et le suivi annuel des transactions du portefeuille, notamment par l’analyse de données qualitatives et quantitatives, de références de GES et de méthodologies d’estimation des émissions. 
 Évaluer l’alignement des transactions avec les objectifs d’impact de FinDev Canada et favoriser l’intégration des considérations d’impact tout au long du cycle d’investissement. 
 Réaliser des évaluations de financement climatique, y compris l’admissibilité climatique, l’analyse des émissions de gaz à effet de serre et les résultats liés au climat. 
 Examiner les méthodologies de comptabilisation du carbone et cerner les occasions d’améliorer la mesure et la déclaration des émissions. 
 Contribuer à l’amélioration des méthodologies, outils, modèles et pratiques de collecte et de mesure des données d’impact. 
 Collaborer avec des collègues des équipes d’investissement, de gestion des risques, des affaires juridiques et d’autres fonctions pour les activités liées aux rapports, aux divulgations et aux relations clients en matière d’impact. 
 Soutenir la préparation de rapports, de présentations et de documents d’information destinés à la haute direction, au conseil d’administration et aux parties prenantes externes. 
 Repérer les occasions de renforcer les résultats d’impact et soutenir les initiatives d’assistance technique lorsque pertinent. 
 Contribuer à l’apprentissage continu, au partage des connaissances et à l’amélioration continue de l’équipe. 
 Responsabilités supplémentaires au niveau Agent(e), Climat et impact 
 Diriger des évaluations d’impact complexes et fournir des conseils relatifs aux enjeux d’impact dans un portefeuille de transactions. 
 Agir à titre de personne-ressource spécialisée en mesure et gestion de l’impact, en égalité des genres ou en sujets liés au climat. 
 Encadrer et soutenir les membres moins expérimentés de l’équipe. 
 Diriger ou coordonner l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre d’améliorations aux processus, méthodologies et pratiques de production de rapports de l’équipe. 
 Profil recherché 
 Diplôme universitaire de premier cycle en économie, sciences de l’environnement, politique climatique, finance durable, développement international, génie ou dans une discipline connexe. 
 Expérience  
 Associé(e) principal(e) (niveau 16) : De 3 à 5 années d’expérience pertinente en financement du développement, finance durable, investissement à impact, mesure de l’impact ou dans un domaine connexe.
 Agent(e) (niveau 17) : Plus de 5 années d’expérience pertinente, avec une capacité démontrée à mener de façon autonome des évaluations d’impact et à gérer des dossiers complexes. 
 Connaissance des pratiques de mesure, de suivi et d’évaluation du climat et de l’impact. 
 Solides compétences analytiques et quantitatives. 
 Excellentes aptitudes en communication écrite, en présentation et en communication interpersonnelle. 
 Capacité à travailler de façon autonome et collaborative dans un environnement dynamique. 
 Bilinguisme dans les deux langues officielles (français et anglais). 
 Ce qui vous permettra de vous démarquer 
 Expérience des évaluations climatiques et d’impact au sein d’institutions financières, d’institutions de financement du développement, de sociétés d’investissement à impact ou de cabinets-conseils. 
 Expérience de vie ou de travail dans des marchés émergents ou des économies en développement. 
 Expérience dans un ou plusieurs secteurs prioritaires de FinDev Canada, notamment les institutions financières, les infrastructures durables, l’agroentreprise, la foresterie ou les chaînes de valeur dans les marchés émergents et les économies en développement. 
 Expérience dans l’élaboration de méthodologies, d’outils ou de systèmes de production de rapports sur l’impact. 
 Compétences avancées en Excel, en analyse de données ou en visualisation de données. 
 Maîtrise de l’espagnol. 
 Connaissance des méthodologies de comptabilisation des GES et des cadres de divulgation liés au climat. 
 Prêt à faire la différence ?

 Department Overview: 
 Our team of trusted audit professionals interact with every part of the Bank to provide strategic guidance and independent oversight.  Safeguarding the reputation of TD's good governance depends on us.

 CUSTOMER 
 Conduct audit work based on established audit plans and execute the audit in accordance with established standards ensuring completion
 Execute testing of controls such as but not limited to walkthroughs (leading and documentation), test scripts (development and execution), and issue management (identification and capturing in the grid)
 May execute the development of Audit Planning Memorandum (APM), Process Risk and Control Matrix (pRCM), Findings Grid and Audit Report.
 May complete L1 reviews/sign off on all audit activities (i.e. walkthroughs, test scripts, test results, grid, evidence uploads)
 Contribute to the audit planning process for specific audits, ensuring appropriate programs and audit risk assessments are completed accordingly
 Manage the ongoing audit communications process with the stakeholders during and subsequent to the audit
 Present objective and independent audit opinion on the adequacy of internal controls in accordance with established professional audit standards, including presentation of findings and recommendations to stakeholders and audit management
 Execute follow-up of findings raised from regulatory and internal divisional audits in accordance with firm policy
 Provide subject matter expertise and/or input to audit projects/initiatives as a representative for area of specialization identify key risks and identify opportunities where controls are missing or are inadequate to mitigate these risks
 SHAREHOLDER 
 Adhere to internal policies / procedures, enterprise frameworks and methodologies and applicable regulatory guidelines, contribute to the review of internal processes and activities and assist in identifying control weaknesses/failures, potential opportunities to improve operational efficiencies for own business area
 May develop and provide complex reporting, analysis, and assessments at the functional or enterprise level
 Prioritize and manage own workload to deliver quality results and meet assigned timelines
 Keep current on emerging trends / developments and grow knowledge of the business, analytical tools and techniques and apply them where appropriate
 Develop and deliver audit findings, presentations / communications to management or broader audience
 Assess / identify key issues and escalate to appropriate levels and relevant stakeholders where required
 Contribute to the analysis, due diligence and implementation of initiatives within defined area of responsibility
 EMPLOYEE / TEAM 
 Continuously enhance knowledge / expertise in own area Support a positive work environment that promotes service to the business, quality, innovation and teamwork and ensure timely communication of issues/ points of interest
 Identify and recommend opportunities to enhance productivity, effectiveness and operational efficiency
 Establish effective relationships across multiple businesses
 Participate in knowledge transfer within the team and business units
 Work to achieve individual goals and support other team members in the achievement of team goals and divisional objectives
 BREADTH & DEPTH 
 Work as an audit subject matter expert and may coach and educate others
 Oversee and/or independently perform audits from end to end
 May lead moderately complex audits and have responsibility for completion of the audit.
 Undertake and complete a variety of projects and initiatives, may include the integration of cross functional processes within own area of expertise
 Ability to process and handle confidential information with discretion.
 Generally, reports to an Audit Group Manager or Senior Audit Group Manager role
 EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION 
 Undergraduate degree required
 5+ years of relevant experience
 CPA considered a strong asset

 Mattel is currently seeking a Manager, Quality Engineering. This role is a member of the corporate Quality Engineering team and is responsible for leading a team of Quality Engineers supporting Mattel Global Brand Teams and product development programs. The Manager will work directly with Marketing, Design, Product Development, other R&D support teams, Quality Data Analytics, Product Safety and Regulatory Compliance, laboratories, and global Manufacturing and Quality teams.
 The Manager, Quality Engineering will provide both people and technical leadership to ensure quality, safety, regulatory compliance, reliability, and consumer expectations are effectively integrated throughout the product development lifecycle. The Manager will shape and execute quality strategies within assigned brands, product categories, or areas of responsibility while developing engineering talent and driving consistent execution of Quality Engineering practices.
 The Manager will have responsibility for team performance, talent development, resource planning, technical execution, and quality outcomes within their assigned scope. This role requires strong technical judgment and the ability to influence cross-functional decisions while building a high-performing Quality Engineering team.
 What Your Impact Will Be: 
 Strategy Development & Execution 
 Shapes and executes Quality Engineering strategies within assigned brands, product categories, or functional areas to support business objectives and consumer expectations.
 Ensures consistent execution of product quality, safety, risk management, reliability, and regulatory requirements throughout the product development lifecycle.
 Maintains a strong understanding of applicable global toy and consumer product regulations, standards, and industry best practices and ensures requirements are effectively understood and implemented by the team.
 Maintains awareness of new and evolving regulatory requirements, standards, technologies, and industry practices and supports implementation of applicable changes within the organization.
 Identifies systemic product and process risks within assigned areas and develops strategies with appropriate cross-functional partners to mitigate those risks.
 Contributes Quality Engineering expertise and lessons learned to the development and improvement of broader organizational practices and processes.
 Leadership & Team Development 
 Leads, coaches, and develops a team of Quality Engineers, building capability in quality systems, regulatory requirements, technical problem-solving, risk management, data analysis, and decision-making.
 Establishes clear goals, priorities, expectations, and accountability for the team and ensures alignment with Quality Engineering and business objectives.
 Provides ongoing coaching, feedback, performance management, and career development for team members.
 Develops technical and leadership capability within the team through mentoring, stretch assignments, knowledge sharing, and development planning.
 Assesses team capability and resource needs and appropriately allocates engineering resources based on product complexity, risk, workload, and business priorities.
 Supports hiring, onboarding, development, succession planning, and retention of Quality Engineering talent.
 Creates an environment that encourages technical curiosity, collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and appropriate escalation of product quality and safety concerns.
 Cross-Functional Influence 
 Builds strong partnerships with Marketing, Design, Product Development, Product Safety, Regulatory Compliance, Quality Data Analytics, Play Labs, Manufacturing, laboratories, and other cross-functional organizations.
 Ensures Quality Engineering is appropriately engaged throughout product development to influence decisions affecting product quality, safety, compliance, reliability, and consumer satisfaction.
 Anticipates downstream impacts, opportunities, and risks and ensures appropriate cross-functional engagement and communication for effective resolution.
 Influences cross-functional teams and leaders to make balanced, risk-based decisions while maintaining consumer safety and regulatory compliance as fundamental requirements.
 Provides Quality Engineering leadership during significant product quality, safety, compliance, manufacturing, and post-market issues.
 Establishes effective communication and escalation practices within the team to ensure significant risks are appropriately communicated to Quality Engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
 Decision-Making & Data Strategy 
 Promotes objective, data-driven decision-making throughout the Quality Engineering team.
 Ensures engineers identify, collect, analyze, and appropriately interpret data needed to support product quality and risk decisions.
 Reviews technical analyses and recommendations for complex or higher-risk issues and ensures conclusions are technically sound, clearly communicated, and appropriately documented.
 Utilizes product testing, consumer complaints, returns, Quality Data Analytics, Play Lab findings, manufacturing performance, and other available data to identify trends, emerging risks, and improvement opportunities.
 Establishes and monitors appropriate KPIs and quality metrics for assigned areas and ensures meaningful trends and issues result in appropriate action.
 Communicates significant quality trends, risks, and recommendations to Quality Engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
 Technical & Engineering Excellence 
 Provides technical leadership and oversight for product investigations, root cause analysis, engineering studies, sampling strategies, risk assessments, product verification, and validation activities.
 Ensures appropriate use of investigation and problem-solving methodologies such as Fishbone diagrams, 5-Why, FMEA, and other applicable root cause analysis tools.
 Provides oversight and guidance for the development and maintenance of Product Requirement Documents (PRDs), Primary Concerns Documents (PCDs), testing strategies, and other Quality Engineering documentation.
 Ensures product concepts, intended play patterns, foreseeable use and misuse, consumer interactions, and identified product risks are appropriately translated into robust testing and verification strategies.
 Partners with internal laboratories and third-party testing organizations to ensure testing strategies appropriately address regulatory requirements, identified risks, and product performance expectations.
 Ensures investigations and corrective actions are thorough, technically sound, appropriately documented, and completed in a timely manner.
 Provides technical guidance on the appropriate application and interpretation of statistical analyses, sampling plans, engineering studies, and quality data.
 Ensures appropriate execution of risk management activities and application of tools such as FMEA, FTA, PHA, and other applicable risk analysis methodologies.
 Maintains a thorough understanding of internal Quality Management System procedures and ensures the team operates in compliance with applicable processes and requirements.
 Product & Consumer Quality 
 Ensures product knowledge, foreseeable consumer use, and play patterns are incorporated into Quality Engineering decisions and product risk assessments.
 Utilizes quality system data, consumer feedback, testing results, product returns, manufacturing performance, and post-market information to understand product and process performance.
 Identifies opportunities to improve product quality, reliability, durability, and consumer satisfaction based on available data and lessons learned.
 Leads or supports investigation and resolution of significant post-market product quality and safety issues within assigned areas.
 Partners with cross-functional teams to ensure lessons learned from consumer and field performance are incorporated into current and future product development.
 Culture & Continuous Improvement

 Identifies and leads continuous improvement initiatives within assigned areas through the appropriate application of continuous improvement methodologies and tools.
 Assesses Quality Engineering processes and identifies opportunities to improve effectiveness, consistency, scalability, and efficiency.
 Leads cross-functional improvement efforts and ensures improvements maintain compliance with regulatory requirements, standards, and internal Quality Management System requirements.
 Uses KPIs, quality metrics, lessons learned, and benchmarking to identify opportunities for improvement.
 Promotes adoption and sharing of best practices across Quality Engineering teams.
 Builds business cases, as appropriate, for significant improvement opportunities and communicates the expected quality, operational, consumer, and business impact.
What We’re Looking For: 
 Exceptional interpersonal and people leadership skills with demonstrated ability to lead, coach, develop, and motivate technical professionals.
 Demonstrated knowledge of consumer product regulatory standards, with an emphasis on toys or children's products.
 Strong technical judgment with the ability to evaluate complex product quality, safety, regulatory, manufacturing, and consumer issues and make sound risk-based decisions.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with demonstrated ability to use data to identify solutions and drive effective actions.
 Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and leaders without direct authority.
 Ability to balance product safety, compliance, quality, consumer experience, business needs, cost, and schedule while maintaining appropriate quality standards.
 Demonstrated ability to effectively manage multiple projects, team priorities, and resources without missing critical deadlines.
 High level of personal and professional integrity and trustworthiness with a strong work ethic, sound judgment, and accountability.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including listening and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex technical issues clearly and concisely.
 Resourceful, diplomatic, and professional, with the ability to build strong relationships across functions, geographies, and organizational levels.
 Collaborative leader with strong results orientation, positive attitude, and demonstrated ability to create accountability while maintaining effective working relationships.

 Adaptable; able to shift priorities and focus as departmental, product development, and business demands change.
 Experience, Education, & Skills: 
 Bachelor's degree in Industrial, Electrical, Mechanical, Materials Engineering, or related technical discipline.
 6+ years of progressive experience in product development, product engineering, manufacturing, or quality roles, preferably within toys, children's products, or consumer products.
 Previous experience leading engineers, technical teams, or significant cross-functional programs; formal people-management experience preferred.
 Working knowledge of global toy and consumer product safety standards and regulatory requirements.
 Strong knowledge of Quality Management System structure, procedures, and implementation.
 Experience with product development processes from concept through production and post-market support.
 Knowledge of risk management principles and tools such as FMEA, FTA, PHA, and other structured risk assessment methodologies.
 Knowledge of engineering and quality tools including statistical analysis, Cause-and-Effect Analysis, root cause analysis, process mapping, sampling methodologies, and engineering studies.
 Experience interpreting quality and product performance data and applying statistical analysis to support engineering decisions.
 Experience working with internal and/or third-party product testing laboratories.
 Experience supporting global manufacturing, suppliers, and product development organizations.
 Knowledge of Human Factors/Usability Engineering principles and their application to toys and consumer products preferred.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office, project management tools, and statistical analysis software such as Minitab.

 - Advanced Excel and financial modelling skills

 - Working knowledge of credit facility mechanics: borrowing bases, advance rates, eligibility criteria and payment waterfalls

 We're looking for a QA Automation Engineer who is passionate about software quality and automation to help ensure our products are reliable, scalable, and deliver an exceptional customer experience.
 The Opportunity
 Today, our automated test coverage is unit tests and some integration testing — we have no systematic automated coverage of end-to-end user flows. That's the gap this role exists to close. You'll design and build our automated E2E testing practice from the ground up, working closely with Product and Engineering to make sure we stop shipping regressions as we scale. You'll have real latitude here: this isn't a role where testing requirements arrive fully formed. Product can tell you what the product needs to do; figuring out how we verify it actually does that reliably is yours to define.
 How We Work
 Decisions live as close to the work as possible — you'll own how testing gets built, not just execute a checklist someone else wrote.
 We're kind, not nice — we say the hard thing early, in a way that respects the person hearing it. Feedback is specific and timely, not saved for a review cycle.
 We ship in small increments and treat real usage as the fastest way to learn what's working.
 We hold strong opinions loosely — bring conviction, stay open to being wrong.
 What you'll be doing 
 Guide Product Managers in translating use cases into testable requirements and edge cases — PMs bring the "what," you bring the "how do we know it actually works."
 Own the definition of test strategy and testing standards, and design our automated E2E / user-flow testing approach from scratch.
 Develop and execute automated functional, regression, integration, and end-to-end test suites.
 Implement the automated portions of the testing plans you define.
 Mentor and train engineers on writing, maintaining, and extending automated tests — part of this role's mandate is building testing capability across the team, not just within QA.
 Perform manual/exploratory testing where automation isn't yet in place.
 Identify, document, and track defects, working with engineering to drive timely resolution.
 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines.
 Monitor test execution, analyze failures, and continuously improve coverage and reliability.
 What You'll Bring
 5+ years of experience in Software Quality Assurance, including 3+ years focused on test automation.
 Experience in testing web applications, APIs, mobile apps and backend services.
 Experience designing an automated testing practice from scratch — not just extending one that already exists.
 Comfort partnering with Product Managers who rely on you to help surface testing needs and edge cases
 Hands-on experience with test automation frameworks (Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or similar).
 Experience testing REST APIs (Postman or similar).
 Proficiency in Python and/or TypeScript; Ruby experience is a plus given our Rails services.
 Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and Agile practices.
 Experience mentoring or upskilling other engineers in testing practices.
 Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills; excellent communication.
 Nice to Have
 Experience with IoT, connected devices, or hardware-interfacing software — this is the environment you'd be working in day to day, though not a requirement.
 Experience with EV charging, OCPP, or similar device-communication protocols.
 Familiarity with AWS, Azure, or GCP.
 Performance or load testing experience.
 A Note on Our Stack
 We're primarily Python and TypeScript, with React on the frontend and some Ruby on Rails services. We're directionally leaning toward Playwright as our automation framework, but that's not locked in — it's unproven at our scale, and if you've got a strong point of view otherwise, we want to hear it.
 Why Join SWTCH?
 You'll be building something that doesn't exist yet at a company where your judgment on how to build it is genuinely trusted, not just tolerated. If you want ownership over a testing practice from day one — and the chance to shape how an engineering team thinks about quality — we'd love to talk.
 Business Impact - As a core member of the team, you have the opportunity to take a supporting role and make a significant impact on the culture and values of the company.
 Environmental Impact - We are a clean energy company with a mission to reduce carbon emissions globally to ensure a clean and sustainable future.
 Diversity - People develop their talents and skills in different ways. We value different paths and experiences. If you think you meet the qualifications we are seeking, take a chance and express your interest here.
 SWTCH does not offer employment to prospects without first ensuring that qualified candidates speak directly with the hiring manager and a member of our P&C team. All qualifications will be done face-to-face, whether that is in person or over Google Meet. SWTCH does not send out offers of employment without meeting candidates and does not offer employment via text. If you are contacted for any personal information via text and/or without having met a member of our hiring team in person, please disregard. 
 SWTCH Energy is an equal opportunity employer, all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

À propos de Mila
 Fondé par le professeur Yoshua Bengio de l’Université de Montréal, Mila rassemble des chercheurs spécialisés en intelligence artificielle et plus précisément en apprentissage automatique, apprentissage profond et apprentissage par renforcement. Reconnu mondialement pour ses importants travaux, Mila s’est particulièrement distingué dans la modélisation du langage, la traduction automatique, la reconnaissance d’objets et les modèles génératifs. Depuis 2017, Mila est le fruit d’une collaboration entre l’Université de Montréal et l’Université McGill, en lien étroit avec Polytechnique Montréal et HEC Montréal.
 Mila s’est donné pour mission d’être un pôle mondial d’avancées scientifiques qui inspire l’innovation et l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle (IA) au bénéfice de tous.
 Pour en connaitre davantage, veuillez consulter https://mila.quebec/ 
 Le Défi
 Mila est à un point d’inflexion : nous tirons parti de notre leadership scientifique pour ancrer et façonner un écosystème mondial de l’IA. L'opérationnalisation de la vision « Mila 3.0 » exige une réflexion stratégique approfondie jumelée à un accompagnement rigoureux des équipes dans la conception, l'introduction et l'évolution de leurs modèles d'affaires ainsi que la rationalisation de leurs processus.
 La personne titulaire du poste de Directeur·trice principal·e, Stratégie et Opérations jouera un rôle clé pour faire évoluer la stratégie d'une planification ponctuelle vers un levier continu d'alignement, d'efficacité et d'impact organisationnel. Relevant du·de la Vice-président·e Stratégie, finances et partenariats, vous agirez comme un·e partenaire stratégique et un moteur d'efficience opérationnelle (BizOps), en étroite collaboration avec vos pairs à la direction, notamment les Directions principales Finances et Talent, afin d'épauler les différentes directions dans la conception et l'introduction de nouvelles initiatives, la modernisation de leurs offres et la structuration de l'exécution entre les fonctions clés.
 Pour y parvenir, vous dirigerez une équipe resserrée composée à l'amorce de deux (2) Conseiller·ère·s principaux·ales en stratégie. Conçue pour maximiser l'impact sans lourdeur structurelle, cette équipe évoluera de façon flexible selon les besoins, en s'appuyant sur des expertises internes ou externes selon le cas, pour soutenir l'ingénierie BizOps, les projets majeurs et le déploiement progressif d'une capacité organisationnelle en gestion de projet, tout en conservant une taille compacte axée sur l'excellence et la rapidité d'exécution. En vous appuyant sur la position fortement transversale et multidisciplinaire de votre rôle, vous exercerez un leadership d'influence pour créer la cohérence, éliminer les goulots d'étranglement opérationnels, instaurer des rituels de gestion rigoureux et accélérer la concrétisation des priorités stratégiques de Mila.
 Principales Responsabilités 
 1. Stratégie et planification intégrée (~35 %)
 Planification stratégique : Diriger l'élaboration de la planification annuelle et pluriannuelle de Mila, en apportant les cadres méthodologiques, les diagnostics et les analyses nécessaires pour structurer la réflexion de la haute direction.
 Cycle de planification annuelle intégrée : En étroite collaboration avec les Directeur·rice·s principaux·ales Finances et Talent, structurer et piloter un cycle de planification annuelle intégrée reliant les priorités stratégiques, le budget et la planification de la main-d'œuvre. Concevoir et déployer un modèle de déclinaison en cascade, du plan stratégique jusqu'aux objectifs des directions et des équipes, appuyé sur des OKR.
 Veille d'écosystème et positionnement stratégique : Assurer une veille stratégique et concurrentielle continue sur les tendances technologiques en IA, les modèles d'innovation mondiaux et les pratiques organisationnelles émergentes, et réaliser des analyses d'écosystème afin d'identifier les secteurs industriels, institutionnels et scientifiques où les initiatives et le transfert technologique de Mila génèrent le plus grand impact, ainsi que de nouvelles avenues de développement et de financement.
 Cas d'affaires et modélisation : Formuler des hypothèses, mener des études de faisabilité et élaborer des dossiers d'affaires rigoureux (analyses de marché, modélisation financière, évaluation d'impact) pour appuyer la prise de décision exécutive lors du lancement de nouvelles initiatives.
 Communication exécutive : Concevoir des synthèses stratégiques, récits percutants et présentations de niveau exécutif destinés au comité de direction, au conseil d'administration et aux partenaires d'envergure.
 2. Exécution de la stratégie et BizOps (~40 %)
 Habilitation de la priorisation du portefeuille : Outiller l'équipe de direction (COO Council) dans l'arbitrage du portefeuille de priorités de Mila : vue consolidée du portefeuille de projets, processus d'accueil et de qualification des nouvelles initiatives, lecture de la capacité par rapport à la demande et scénarios d'arbitrage. S'assurer que les décisions se traduisent concrètement dans l'exécution.
 Pilotage des priorités et suivi stratégique : Définir avec pragmatisme les indicateurs essentiels de succès (en collaboration avec l’équipe BI) pour donner une visibilité claire sur l'avancement de la stratégie, sans alourdir l'opérationnel. Exercer un leadership transversal pour fluidifier les échanges entre équipes et débloquer les dépendances.
 Cadence d'exécution et rituels de gestion : Instaurer une gouvernance d'exécution rigoureuse (ex. Quarterly Business Reviews, protocoles d'alignement et SLAs inter-équipes) pour accroître la vélocité opérationnelle.
 Standardisation des modes opératoires : Définir et déployer des structures de fonctionnement, des critères de jalonnage (stage-gates) et des règles de livraison claires pour opérationnaliser les nouvelles initiatives transversales.
 Optimisation des processus transversaux : Cartographier, simplifier et optimiser les flux de travail interfonctionnels critiques de l'organisation. L'objectif est de renforcer les synergies, d'éliminer les redondances et de résorber les goulots d'étranglement pour faciliter la collaboration entre équipes dans un contexte de croissance et de changement rapide.
 Capacité en gestion de projet : Structurer progressivement la capacité de gestion de projet de Mila (méthodes, outils et gabarits communs, suivi de portefeuille, accompagnement et communauté de pratique) afin de répondre à la demande croissante des équipes, en s'appuyant sur des ressources internes ou externes selon le cas. Piloter directement un nombre limité d'initiatives stratégiques transversales majeures.
 3. Soutien à la conception d'initiatives et de modèles (~25 %)
 Accompagnement à la conception d'initiatives et de modèles : Agir comme ressource stratégique auprès des directeur·rice·s des différentes équipes de Mila, et qui demeurent responsables de leurs offres et programmes, dans la conception, l'évolution et l'introduction de nouveaux modèles, programmes et initiatives d'envergure (ex. modèles d'engagement et de partenariat, grands projets d'IA, programmes d'éducation et de formation). Apporter structuration, modélisation d'affaires et conception des modes de livraison pour favoriser leur alignement stratégique et leur scalabilité.
 Scolarité et formation : Baccalauréat en administration des affaires, économie, finance, ingénierie ou domaine pertinent. Une maîtrise (MBA, M.Sc.) est considérée comme un atout majeur.
 Expérience : Au moins 10 années d’expérience pertinente, dont une expérience significative (idéalement 5 ans ou plus) dans un rôle interne de stratégie, d’opérations stratégiques (BizOps) ou de chef·fe de cabinet, ainsi qu’une expérience confirmée en gestion d’équipe.
 Prise en charge de bout en bout (End-to-End Ownership) : Capacité démontrée à piloter des initiatives stratégiques sur l'ensemble de leur cycle de vie, de la conception stratégique initiale et l'élaboration du cas d'affaires jusqu'à la mise en place des processus, des modes opératoires et des modèles de livraison.
 Gestion et leadership transversal : Expérience confirmée en gestion d'équipe multidisciplinaire et de partenaires externes, et capacité démontrée à exercer un leadership d'influence en environnement matriciel (mobilisation sans autorité hiérarchique directe auprès des départements RH, Marketing, Solutions IA, Finances, etc.), incluant une étroite collaboration avec les pairs (Finances, Talent, etc.) en matière de planification intégrée.
 Analyse et vision stratégique : Solide expertise en planification stratégique, veille de marché, formulation d'hypothèses, modélisation financière et élaboration de cas d'affaires (business cases) structurés et quantifiés.
 Ingénierie de processus et BizOps : Expérience démontrée dans la cartographie et l'optimisation de flux de travail (workflows), l'implantation de cadences de gestion (SBR/QBR) et de cadres OKR, et l'élimination de goulots d'étranglement opérationnels. Une expérience dans la structuration de la gestion de portefeuille ou d'une capacité en gestion de projet (PMO), y compris par l'entremise de partenaires externes, constitue un atout.
 Conception et transformation d'offres : Expérience dans le soutien stratégique à la conception et à la structuration de nouveaux modèles d'affaires, de structures de partenariat, de projets d'IA d'envergure ou de programmes de formation.
 Langues : Maîtrise professionnelle du français et de l'anglais (écrit et parlé) requise.
 De bonnes raisons pour travailler à Mila
 L’occasion de contribuer à une mission unique avec un impact important;
 Un programme d’assurance collective complet (maladie, dentaire, invalidité, vie, assurance voyage et garanties complémentaires);
 Un programme d’aide aux employés et à la famille;
 Un accès à un service de télémédecine;
 Une politique de congés annuels offrant une base de 20 jours de vacances dès l’embauche;
 Un régime d’épargne retraite avec contribution de l’employeur minimale de 4%;
 Une généreuse enveloppe flexible vous permettant de personnaliser vos avantages sociaux en fonction de ce qui contribue à votre bien-être;
 Un horaire flexible, un horaire d’été et une possibilité de télétravail;
 Un milieu de travail au cœur de la Petite Italie, dans le quartier branché Mile-Ex, à proximité des transports en commun;
 Une équipe d’experts de leur domaine, des gens passionnés et passionnants;
 Une ambiance de travail collaborative et inclusive.
 Nous voulons vous connaître
 À Mila, la diversité nous tient à cœur. Nous valorisons un environnement de travail équitable, ouvert et respectueux des différences. Nous encourageons toute personne souhaitant œuvrer dans un écosystème en progression continue et stimulée à contribuer à l’application et la définition d’une culture saine et inclusive, à postuler.
 Veuillez noter que seules les personnes sélectionnées seront contactées.

 About Mila
 Founded by Professor Yoshua Bengio of the Université de Montréal, Mila brings together researchers specializing in artificial intelligence, and more specifically in machine learning, deep learning and reinforcement learning. Recognized worldwide for its important contributions to the field of deep learning, Mila has particularly distinguished itself in language modeling, machine translation, object recognition and generative models. Since 2017, Mila has been the fruit of a collaboration between Université de Montréal and McGill University, with close links to Polytechnique Montréal and HEC Montréal.
 Mila's mission is to be a global hub of scientific advances that inspires innovation and the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) for the benefit of all.
 To find out more, please visit https://mila.quebec/ 
 The challenge
 Mila is at an inflection point: we are leveraging our scientific leadership to anchor and shape a global AI ecosystem. Operationalizing the “Mila 3.0” vision requires deep strategic thinking combined with rigorous support for teams in designing, introducing, and evolving their business models, as well as streamlining their processes.
 The Senior Director, Strategy and Operations will play a key role in evolving strategy from a periodic planning exercise into an ongoing driver of alignment, efficiency, and organizational impact. Reporting to the Vice-President, Strategy, Finance & Partnerships, you will act as a strategic partner and an engine of operational efficiency (BizOps), working hand in hand with your peer senior directors, notably Finance and Talent, to support the various teams in shaping and introducing new initiatives, modernizing their offerings, and structuring execution across key functions.
 To achieve this, you will lead a lean team initially composed of two (2) Senior Strategy Advisors. Designed to maximize impact without structural weight, this team will evolve flexibly with needs, drawing on internal or external expertise as appropriate, to support BizOps engineering, major projects and the progressive build-out of an enterprise project management capability, while maintaining a compact size focused on excellence and speed of execution. Leveraging the highly cross-functional and multidisciplinary nature of your role, you will lead through influence to build coherence, eliminate operational bottlenecks, establish rigorous management rhythms, and accelerate the realization of Mila's strategic priorities.
 Main responsibilities
 1. Strategy and Integrated Planning (~35%)
 Strategic planning: Lead the development of Mila's annual and multi-year planning, providing the necessary methodological frameworks, diagnostics, and analyses to structure executive leadership reflection.
 Integrated annual planning cycle: In close collaboration with the Senior Directors of Finance and Talent, structure and run an integrated annual planning cycle linking strategic priorities, budget and workforce planning. Design and deploy a cascading model from the strategic plan to departmental and team objectives and OKRs.
 Ecosystem intelligence and strategic positioning: Maintain continuous strategic and competitive intelligence on AI technology trends, global innovation models and emerging organizational practices, and perform ecosystem analyses to identify the industrial, institutional and scientific sectors where Mila's initiatives and technology transfer generate the greatest impact and new avenues of development.
 Business cases and modeling: Formulate hypotheses, conduct feasibility studies, and build rigorous business cases (market analyses, financial modeling, impact assessment) to support executive decision-making when launching new initiatives.
 Executive communication: Design strategic summaries, compelling narratives, and executive-level presentations intended for the executive committee, the board of directors, and major partners.
 2. Strategy Execution and BizOps (~40%)
 Portfolio prioritization enablement: Equip the executive team (COO Council) to arbitrate Mila's portfolio of priorities: a consolidated project portfolio view, an intake process for new initiatives, a capacity-vs-demand view and trade-off scenarios. Ensure decisions are followed through in execution.
 Steering priorities and strategic tracking: Pragmatically define key success indicators (in collaboration with the BI team) to provide clear visibility on strategic progress without overburdening operations. Exercise cross-functional leadership to streamline interactions between teams and unblock dependencies.
 Execution cadence and management rhythms: Establish rigorous execution governance (e.g., Quarterly Business Reviews, alignment protocols, and inter-team SLAs) to increase operational velocity.
 Standardizing operating procedures: Define and deploy operating structures, stage-gate criteria, and clear delivery rules to operationalize new cross-functional initiatives.
 Optimizing cross-functional processes: Map, simplify, and optimize the organization's critical cross-functional workflows. The goal is to strengthen synergies, eliminate redundancies, and resolve bottlenecks to facilitate collaboration among teams in a context of rapid growth and change.
 Project management capability: Progressively structure Mila's project management capability (shared methods, tools and templates, portfolio tracking, coaching and a community of practice) to meet growing demand from teams, drawing on internal or external resources as appropriate. Directly lead a limited number of major cross-functional strategic initiatives.
 3. Support for Initiative and Model Design (~25%)
 Initiative and model design support: Act as a strategic resource for the directors of Mila’s various teams, who remain accountable for their offerings and programs, in shaping, evolving and introducing new models, programs and large-scale initiatives (e.g., engagement and partnership models, major AI projects, education and training programs). Contribute structuring, business modeling and delivery design to support their strategic alignment and scalability.
 Your profile
 Education and training: Bachelor's degree in business administration, economics, finance, engineering, or a related field. A master's degree (MBA, M.Sc.) is considered a major asset.
 Experience: At least 10 years of relevant experience, including significant experience (ideally 5 years or more) in an in-house strategy, strategic operations (BizOps) or chief of staff role, as well as proven team management experience.
 End-to-End Ownership: Demonstrated ability to lead strategic initiatives throughout their entire lifecycle, from initial strategic design and business case development to the implementation of processes, operating models, and delivery models.
