You build automated testing frameworks that are reliable, easy to maintain, and ready to grow with the business. And you’re always looking for ways to make the whole thing work better.
 If that sounds like your kind of work, we’ve got a friendly team, plenty of technical challenges, and a meaningful mission we’d love you to be part of. Let’s chat!
 AlgaeCal is on the lookout for a Senior QA Developer to bring their skills to our lively QA team and help transform lives, one stable release at a time.
 Small print here ⇒ We’re an eCommerce company. So, we want you to have eCommerce experience. Lots of it. You’ll be helping us improve the quality, stability, and reliability of our React-based storefront and internal middleware. So if automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, and digital marketing technology don’t light at least a small fire in your belly, you probably shouldn’t read any further.
 Still here? Okay then…
 This job might be for you if you’ve got… 
 3+ years of QA development experience. You’ve built, maintained, and improved automated testing strategies, and you can tell us what worked, what didn’t, and what you changed along the way.
 Strong JavaScript and TypeScript skills. You’re comfortable getting into the code, writing reliable automated tests, and coming back six months later without wondering what on earth you were thinking.
 Hands-on experience with Cypress, Playwright, or similar testing frameworks. You know how to investigate unreliable tests, improve coverage, and keep a growing test suite running smoothly.
 The ability to build testing frameworks that can grow with the business. You think about how everything fits together, how easy it is to maintain, and whether it’ll still do the job as things get more complex. You’ll put that thinking to work across our Shopify Hydrogen storefront and backend middleware.
 Experience integrating automated tests into cloud-based CI/CD pipelines. You know how to get the right checks running at the right time, so developers get useful feedback quickly and releases move forward with fewer headaches.
 A good handle on quality reporting. Test coverage, execution times, pipeline stability, recurring failures, and bugs reaching production. You can use those numbers to explain how things are going and where we need to improve.
 Experience testing APIs and investigating performance. API contract testing, load testing, and browser developer tools should be familiar territory. When something slows down or stops behaving, you know where to start looking.
 A few extra tools in your kit. Experience with Python, PHP, Figma, Storybook, or Jest would earn you a few bonus points. You don’t need the full set, so tell us what you’ve worked with.

 Other Qualities You’ll Need

 You’re people smart — in the sense that you’re a great teammate

 Joignez-vous à l’équipe d’EDC ! 
 À EDC, nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. Nous leur offrons les outils financiers et l’expertise dont elles ont besoin pour explorer de nouveaux marchés et réduire les risques, dans un seul but : bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce. 
 Poste : Analyste des risques ou analyste principale des risques/analyste principal des risques, Évaluation des risques et gestion du portefeuille, niveaux  17 à 19 
 Type d’emploi : Affectation permanente/ contractuelle
 Détails de la rémunération : 
 Gestion des risques de portefeuille 17 : Les salaires annuels varient généralement de 84 698 $ à 112 931 $, plus une rémunération au rendement, en fonction des qualifications et de l’expérience. 
 Gestion des risques de portefeuille 18 : Les salaires annuels varient généralement de 96 557 $ à 128 743 $, plus une rémunération au rendement, en fonction des qualifications et de l’expérience. 
 Gestion des risques de portefeuille 19 : Les salaires annuels varient généralement de 112 006 $ à 149 341 $, plus une rémunération au rendement, en fonction des qualifications et de l’expérience. 
 Veuillez noter que la rémunération au rendement ne s’applique qu’aux postes permanents. 
 Lieu de travail 
 Exportation et développement Canada évolue dans un environnement de travail hybride, avec une exigence actuelle de présence au bureau de deux jours par semaine, laquelle passera à trois jours par semaine à compter de septembre 2026 (sous réserve de modifications) .
 La personne choisie peut travailler à partir du siège social d’EDC à Ottawa ou à partir du Carrefour communautaire à Toronto, ou à Montréal.
 Une aide à la réinstallation est offerte aux candidats et candidates admissibles ( ne s’applique qu’aux postes permanents. )
 Candidats internes, veuillez consulter la page Service Now intitulée « Mouvements internes - ce que vous devez savoir ». 
 À propos d’EDC 
 À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. En tant que société d’État à vocation financière, EDC propose des solutions financières innovantes et des conseils d’experts pour aider les entreprises à explorer de nouveaux marchés, à atténuer leurs risques et à se développer.
 Pourquoi vous joindre à EDC? 
 Gamme complète d’avantages sociaux : EDC offre un régime de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux concurrentiel, une bonne conciliation travail-vie personnelle et la chance de contribuer à bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce.
 Conciliation travail-vie personnelle : EDC offre un régime concurrentiel en ce qui concerne la rémunération et la conciliation travail-vie personnelle : différentes options de travail hybride, trois à quatre semaines de vacances, une période de fermeture, des vendredis d’été raccourcis et les vendredis sans réunion.
 Perfectionnement professionnel : Profitez de nos occasions d’apprentissage continu, notamment des programmes de formation, des ateliers et de la formation linguistique.
 Culture inclusive : Intégrez un milieu de travail diversifié et inclusif qui lutte pour l’équité en matière d’emploi et valorise la diversité des idées, des forces et des origines pour favoriser la réussite.
 Programmes de bien-être : Nous offrons des initiatives de bien-être, de l’aide à la santé mentale et des programmes de conditionnement physique pour veiller à votre santé et à votre bonheur.
 Investissement dans la collectivité : Participez à des activités de bénévolat et donnez au suivant grâce à un éventail de programmes de responsabilité sociale.
 Aperçu de l’équipe : 
 L’Équipe de l’évaluation des risques et de la gestion du portefeuille surveille le portefeuille d’assurances en procédant à une évaluation des risques de crédit et à la gestion du portefeuille de façon indépendante, tout en veillant à ce que les mesures appropriées soient prises lorsque le risque de crédit d’une entreprise n’est plus jugé acceptable. Elle participe également à l’examen continu des normes d’octroi et de vérification du crédit et des politiques et procédures en matière d’acceptation des risques du Groupe des assurances. 
 L’Équipe est à la recherche de professionnels du crédit dynamiques et motivés pour gérer un portefeuille d’acheteurs en évaluant les risques de crédit et les risques financiers de façon indépendante afin de déterminer l’acceptation du risque commercial et les capacités de remboursement de ces entreprises, en appui au programme d’assurance d’EDC. 
 Ce que vous ferez : 
 Procéder à des contrôles préalables et aux analyses nécessaires afin d’évaluer la solvabilité et le niveau de risque d’un acheteur ou d’une transaction selon la situation financière en question et d’autres facteurs comme la conjoncture économique du pays et les modalités de paiement.  
 Évaluer les nouvelles demandes de crédit. 
 Assurer une surveillance adéquate et un suivi rapide du portefeuille d’acheteurs pour veiller à ce que les dossiers soient à jour et réduire au minimum les délais relatifs à l’octroi de crédit. 
 Analyser et commenter les développements entourant les secteurs, les marchés et les portefeuilles. 
 Observer en tout temps les normes de crédit reconnues pour disposer des documents nécessaires, mener de bonnes analyses de crédit, et recommander les décisions appropriées. 
 Préparer les évaluations de crédit et présenter des recommandations aux approbateurs de crédit disposant de l’autorité appropriée. 
 Transmettre activement son savoir sectoriel et industriel pour soutenir les équipes sectorielles, les partenaires internes et les clients. 
 S’informer sur les pratiques générales en matière de souscription en assurance crédit. 
 Veiller au respect des règles entourant l’intégrité des données. 
 Assurer la liaison avec les acheteurs, les banques, les fournisseurs d’information et d’autres entités afin d’évaluer les questions relatives au crédit. 
 Apporter continuellement de nouvelles idées d’amélioration pour EDC en travaillant en étroite collaboration avec ses collègues, avec les clients et avec les principaux intermédiaires. Contribuer aux projets ponctuels liés au processus et à d’autres améliorations. 
 Analyste principale des risques ou analyste principal des risques (Gestion des risques de portefeuille 19) – autres responsabilités 
 Posséder une connaissance vaste et approfondie des questions de crédit dans les secteurs concernés et formuler des recommandations en temps utile pour atténuer les risques. 
 Diriger de façon proactive tous les aspects de la gestion du portefeuille, y compris la collecte, l’analyse et la communication efficace des données, ce qui comprend la présentation d’information aux parties prenantes et aux comités pertinents.​ 
 Cultiver un réseau de parties prenantes, en interne et à l’extérieur de la Société, dans l’optique d’améliorer la gestion du portefeuille, s’il y a lieu, de manière à assurer la réussite des projets. 
 Ce que nous cherchons: 
 Diplôme universitaire de premier cycle en comptabilité, en administration des affaires, en finance ou dans un domaine connexe 
 Expérience en gestion du risque de crédit et en commerce international ou dans des domaines connexes, selon l’échelle suivante : 
 Gestion des risques de portefeuille 17 – au moins 5 ans d’expérience 
 Gestion des risques de portefeuille 18 – au moins 7 ans d’expérience 
 Gestion des risques de portefeuille 19 – au moins 9 ans d’expérience 
 Connaissance des principes et des pratiques de gestion du risque de crédit 
 Ce qui vous distinguera : 
 Titre professionnel ou titre en cours d’obtention (CFA, CPA, MBA) 
 Connaissance des pratiques d’évaluation du crédit et de prêt des banques 
 Connaissance des pratiques commerciales internationales et du commerce international 
 Maîtrise des deux langues officielles 
 Admissibilité : 
 EDC s'engage à respecter des pratiques d'emploi équitables et la préférence sera accordée aux candidats qui sont en mesure de travailler légalement au Canada au moment de la présentation de leur candidature (citoyens canadiens ou résidents permanents). Les candidats doivent satisfaire aux exigences de sécurité du gouvernement. Le poste est ouvert aux personnes qui répondent à toutes les exigences essentielles énoncées ci-dessus et dont la candidature est reçue avant la date limite.
 Le poste est ouvert aux personnes qui répondent à toutes les conditions essentielles énoncées ci-dessus et qui soumettent leur demande avant la date de clôture. Vous voulez changer les choses? Saisissez l’occasion d’intégrer une équipe dynamique en pleine croissance et de laisser votre marque dans notre organisation, le domaine du financement du développement et le monde.
 Postulez dès aujourd’hui!
 Vous souhaitez en savoir plus sur EDC? Consultez notre site Web à https://www.edc.ca 
 Engagement d’EDC envers l’équité en matière d’emploi 
 Exportation et développement Canada (EDC) s’engage à favoriser l’équité en matière d’emploi et à constituer une main-d’œuvre diversifiée. Elle s’engage à créer un environnement sûr et inclusif qui respecte les personnes de toutes les origines, aptitudes et compétences. EDC favorise une culture d’inclusion et d’appartenance où chaque personne a des chances égales de se perfectionner, de se développer, de réussir et de réaliser son plein potentiel. 
 Votre candidature doit démontrer clairement que vous répondez à toutes les exigences. Nous remercions tous les candidats de l'intérêt qu'ils portent à une carrière à EDC. Toutefois, seules les personnes sélectionnées pour un entretien seront contactées. Veuillez noter que les candidats qualifiés peuvent être pris en considération pour des postes similaires à ce niveau au sein d'EDC.
 EDC reconnaît que le fait de divulguer la nécessité de prévoir des mesures d’adaptation peut être une question personnelle. Sachez qu’en tant qu’organisation, nous nous engageons à respecter la confidentialité et à veiller à ce que toutes les mesures d’adaptation fournies soient adaptées à vos besoins. Notre objectif est de vous garantir une expérience positive et satisfaisante tout au long du processus de recrutement. N’hésitez donc pas à nous contacter directement pour toute demande d’adaptation à l’adresse accessibility@edc.ca . Nous sommes là pour vous aider à chaque étape du processus.
 Énoncé de confidentialité 
 En postulant à cet emploi, vous reconnaissez avoir lu et compris l'Énoncé de confidentialité d’EDC pour les candidats à l’emploi , qui décrit comment nous recueillons, utilisons, conservons et protégeons les renseignements personnels pendant le processus de recrutement, ainsi que vos droits d’accès et de rectification.

Your Moneris Career - The Opportunity 
 As the Senior Manager, Corporate-Commercial Credit, you will lead a team of Senior Credit Analysts responsible for managing Moneris’ commercial credit risk portfolio, including Large Key Accounts (LAKA), Strategic Partners, and higher-risk Small and Medium Business (SMB) clients. 
 You will oversee underwriting, portfolio monitoring, and risk mitigation activities that support business growth while maintaining risk within established appetite. Partnering with leaders across the organization, you will leverage data, analytics, and industry insights to guide risk-based decision-making, strengthen portfolio performance, and enhance Moneris’ credit risk framework.
 Location: You will be based in our Etobicoke office, balancing in-office collaboration with remote flexibility.
 Reporting Relationship : You will report to the VP, Merchant Portfolio Risk Management.
 Posting Type: Replacement.
 Salary Range: The expected base salary range for this role is $132,000 - $172,000.
 Total compensation may also include variable or discretionary incentive components, including but not limited to bonuses and commissions. Individual job offers are determined by various factors, including experience, education, skills, certifications, and other business needs. 
 Your Moneris Career - What you'll do 
 Lead the Corporate-Commercial credit team to ensure portfolio performance remains within established risk appetite and key metrics, including portfolio growth, attrition, concentration, distribution trends, and loss provisions.
 Lead, develop, and coach a team of Senior Credit Analysts, providing performance management, development opportunities, and guidance on complex credit decisions and risk assessments.
 Identify and remove obstacles to performance and explain how performance expectations align with business priorities.
 Ensure the team decisions within policies, standards, guidelines and is applying risk judgement across the controls
 Manage service levels for the deals, renewals pipeline within credit risk-appetite and performance targets.
 Ensure the controls remain adequate within the 3LODs -lines of defense.
 Execute as an approver for management $ limits and delegate $ limit approval authority across the team.
 Be the first contact for escalation and lead deal flow execution, ensuring timely adjudication, removing pipeline bottlenecks, and enabling efficient decision-making to support revenue realization.
 Apply credit risk models, data analytics, external risk indicators, and industry best practices to support underwriting decisions and portfolio oversight.
 Monitor economic conditions, industry trends, and emerging risks, and implement appropriate mitigation strategies to address potential portfolio impacts.
 Oversee collateral management, high-risk industry reviews, risk rating methodologies, and counterparty credit assessments using tools such as FRISK, Moody’s KMV, S&P Capital IQ, and proprietary risk models.
 Enhance credit risk processes, controls, and governance practices that support the identification, assessment, monitoring, and management of portfolio risk.
 Partner with LAKA Sales, Strategic Partners, and ISO channels to structure credit solutions, negotiate underwriting terms, and support business growth while maintaining sound risk management practices.
 Manage relationships with Moneris’ largest and most strategically important clients, negotiating credit arrangements, security structures, and covenant requirements.
 Execute outmost professionalism with clients-partners on all aspects of Moneris’ risk oversight program to fit risk appetite while maintaining a competitive market approach. 
 Negotiate with client C-suite level to structure and negotiate appropriate Credit terms and agreement conditions to win new business and maintain competitive market practice-risk appetite. 
 Collaborate with Audit, Legal, Payment Card Schemes, and risk management partners to strengthen controls, address regulatory changes, and support enterprise risk management objectives.
 Maintain and evolve reporting and insights on portfolio performance, key risk indicators (KRIs), key performance indicators (KPIs), and emerging risks to Credit Risk leadership and the Audit and Risk Review Committee (ARRC).
 Contribute to enterprise initiatives and change programs to ensure credit risk requirements are incorporated into business and technology strategies.
 Your Moneris Career - What you bring 
 Required skills and experience 
 Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or equivalent professional experience.
 Professional designation in good standing such as CPA, CFA, CCP, FCSI, or another CSI Institute designation.
 8-10 years of experience in credit risk management within financial services, banking, or payments.
 8-10 years of experience in financial statement analysis, audit, restructuring, workout, or insolvency management.
 5+ years of people leadership experience within a credit risk function.
 Advanced knowledge of data analytics, statistics, Excel, SPSS, SQL, and MATLAB.
 Experience developing and implementing credit risk strategies, portfolio management initiatives, and risk appetite frameworks.
 Experience managing complex client relationships and negotiating corporate-commercial credit terms, mitigation and financial covenants.
 Experience presenting portfolio risk assessments, credit decisions, and business recommendations to senior leaders and executive stakeholders.
 Experience that would set you apart 
 Experience in payment systems and the merchant acquiring industry.
 MBA.
 Bilingualism.
 Your Moneris Career - What you get 
 At Moneris, we believe in empowering you to succeed—personally and professionally. As part of our team, you'll have access to resources, opportunities, and an inclusive environment that supports your development and career.
 Comprehensive Total Rewards Program, including performance-based bonuses, flexible benefits starting from day one, and your choice of a health spending account (HSA) or personal spending account (PSA).
 Retirement planning support, with profit-sharing programs including company match and a defined contribution pension plan.
 Growth & development opportunities, including unlimited access to Coursera, mentorship programs, and an internal gig marketplace.
 Holistic wellness support, with an Employee & Family Assistance Program, 24/7 virtual healthcare, and workplace wellness initiatives.
 Flexibility that works for you, including hybrid work arrangements, a Work from Abroad program, and paid time off programs.

Who We Are: 
At Giant Tiger, our mission is simple: help Canadians save more every day. We’re a Canadian institution rooted in our communities and built on 60+ years of success. Our store teams are the heart of our mission, making sure every customer has a great experience and finds the products they need at the right price.
We’re looking for friendly, driven leaders who love retail, enjoy developing people, and want to grow their careers beyond store management — this posting represents a current opportunity to join Giant Tiger as a Franchisee-in-Training.
 About This Role: 
 Giant Tiger is a proudly Canadian-owned retailer committed to being Canada's place to save more. We're seeking future franchise store owners who thrive in retail and want to lead their stores with passion and a vision. Our Store Owners are leaders who shape their store’s identity, drive success, and positively impact their communities.
 We're looking for entrepreneurial leaders eager to grow their careers and make a difference. Our Franchisee in Training Program offers hands-on training with experienced operators, exposure to diverse markets, and the chance to manage your own store upon completion. Mobility and commitment to community are key. If you are ready to take charge of your own store, we want to hear from you!
 Successful candidates will complete their training within the Northwest New Brunswick region, not limited to the exact cities listed in the title.
 Due to many stores in this region being only French or only English speaking, we do require the incumbent to be fully bilingual. 
 Workplace Arrangements: 
 Working hours: Must be available to work evenings, weekends and holidays, as required. 
 Travel: Must be willing to travel within the assigned region. Occasional overnight travel to our Home Office in Ottawa as well as other stores will be required.
 Region: The specific store within the region will be discussed during the first interviews, and generally, work will take place within 100km of that store unless applying to stores outside the region after completing the program.
 What Giant Tiger Brings: 
 Competitive salary reflective of market rates
 Bonus Plan
 Comprehensive training and continuous learning
 Paid Vacation Time
 Flexible Health Benefits as of day 1
 Employee discount at Giant Tiger Stores
 What you will be doing:   
 In-Class Learning: 
 Complete all training modules and assigned projects during the Franchisee in Training Program.
 Engage in formal mentorship to develop entrepreneurial and leadership skills.
 On-the-Job Learning: 
 Participate in in-store experiences with leaders and their teams.
 Shadow current Franchisees across various regions in Canada.
 Work closely with staff and interact with customers in the community.
 Gain hands-on experience in: Store Management
 Staff Management
 Administration and Reporting
 Community Engagement
 What You’ll Bring:

You turn scrollers into followers… and followers into customers. You know how to make people stop, watch, follow, click… and buy. Likes are nice. Views are nice. But sales are nicer. Because great organic social doesn’t just build an audience. It earns attention, builds trust, and turns that trust into measurable revenue.
 If that sounds like you, you might have what it takes to become our next Organic Social Specialist. 
 Small Print ⇒ We’re not looking for a “like junkie.” We want someone who knows how to grow a social audience and turn that attention into sales. Someone who understands that followers, views, and engagement are only useful if they build trust, drive traffic, and ultimately help customers buy. If you measure success by views alone then this probably isn’t the role for you.
 Still here?
 Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels: 
 We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your work will help more women discover those solutions. You’ll help us become a brand these women actually want to follow. You’ll help create the posts that make her stop. The videos she sends to a friend. The content that makes her think, “Finally. Someone actually gets it.”
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than here.
 This job might be for you if… 
 You understand what makes people stop scrolling . Hooks. Thumbnails. First frames. Captions. Curiosity. Emotion. Pattern interrupts. Trends. You don’t need someone to explain why the first two seconds of a TikTok matter. You already spend more time than is probably healthy wondering why one piece of content gets 327 views while another gets 327,000.
 You know every platform speaks a slightly different language. TikTok isn’t Instagram. Instagram isn’t Facebook. YouTube isn’t Reddit. And taking the exact same post, resizing it four times, and calling it a “social strategy” makes a small part of you die inside. You know how to adapt an idea to the platform, audience, format, and reason somebody is there in the first place.
 You can actually create the stuff. We’re not looking for someone who just sits in meetings talking about content pillars. You’ll help develop ideas, write briefs, schedule content, coordinate assets, get everything live, and make sure the little details don’t fall through the cracks.
 You’ve got a nose for a good trend. Sounds. Formats. Memes. Conversations. Creators. Questions people suddenly can’t stop asking. You pay attention to what’s happening online and can tell the difference between a trend we should jump on… and one that will make a women’s health company look like someone’s dad discovered TikTok.
 You’re obsessed with the audience. What are women talking about? What are they frustrated by? What are they asking in the comments? What myths keep popping up? What are competitors saying? What language are real women actually using? You know some of the best content ideas won’t come from a brainstorm. They’ll come from listening.
 You care about results more than vanity metrics. Followers and likes are lovely. But you also want to know what people clicked, what sent traffic to the site, what converted, what content assisted a sale, and what we should do differently next month. Because ultimately, we’re not trying to win a trophy for “nicest Instagram grid.”
 Numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. Reach. Engagement. Clicks. Conversion. Follower growth. Traffic. UTMs. GA4. You don’t have to be a data scientist wearing six monitors and muttering about statistical significance. But you should be able to look at performance, spot patterns, and turn what you learn into better content.
 You know how to use social scheduling tools without needing an emergency tutorial. Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Later, Buffer, or something similar. We don’t care which logo you’ve stared at most. We care that you understand how to plan, schedule, organize, and manage a social calendar without everything descending into chaos.
 You can turn performance into strategy. You don’t just send a monthly report containing 17 charts and the groundbreaking observation that “engagement was up.” You ask why. What worked? What flopped? Which topics got attention? Which formats drove clicks? What should we do more of? Less of? Test next? The report is only useful if it changes what we do.
 You’re organised enough to keep a lot of little moving pieces moving. Content calendars. Briefs. Designers. Video. Approvals. Links. UTMs. Scheduling. Launch dates. Reporting. Somebody has to keep track of it all. Preferably without sending 14 Slack messages asking, “Any update on this?”
 You play nicely with others. You’ll work with Content, Creative, Acquisition, Email, Influencer, Customer Service and other teams across the business. Sometimes you’ll need something from them. Sometimes they’ll need something from you. You communicate clearly, follow up, solve problems, and understand that being easy to work with is a genuine career superpower.
 You know social never stops changing . Algorithm updates. New features. New formats. Social commerce. Search behaviour. Yesterday’s “best practice” suddenly dying a very public death. You’re curious enough to keep learning without somebody having to chase you around the office waving an industry newsletter.
 You’ve got at least a year of experience in social media marketing or something closely related. Maybe you’ve managed brand accounts. Maybe you’ve built social for an ecommerce company. Maybe you’ve helped grow a community, supported creator campaigns, or owned organic content as part of a broader marketing role. What matters most is that you can show us you’ve done the work and learned from it.
 Women’s health genuinely interests you. You don’t need to arrive knowing everything about women’s health. But you do need to care enough to learn. We’re talking about real health concerns affecting millions of women, so curiosity, empathy, accuracy, and good judgment matter.
 Bonus points if you’ve worked with Shopify, ecommerce brands, Google Sheets, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools.
 Double bonus points if you already have strong opinions about why most brand TikToks are painfully boring.
 Now, time to be honest… is this really you?
 If you’ve already started thinking about what you’d post first, which competitors you’d stalk, and how you’d build our first 10,000 followers…
 We should probably talk. 
 We don’t expect you to know everything. This isn’t a “12 years of TikTok experience required” job ad. But we do want somebody curious, switched on, commercially minded, organised, and hungry to get very, very good at organic social.
 And someone who sees a brand starting from scratch and thinks:
 Ohhh… this could be fun. 
 Other Qualities You’ll Need
 We’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble — you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own.
 You’re hungry — you want to learn more, improve, and keep getting better.
 You’re people-smart — in the sense that you’re a great teammate.
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at our company.
 So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that’s a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?
 We believe in rewarding top talent.
 So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills, curiosity, and hunger to grow, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 An incredible dog-friendly office
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave.
 Culture is everything to us.
 Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible.
 But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply
 So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of Team AlgaeCal?
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer the right person.
 So, to make sure our future Organic Social Specialist is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive here, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application.

 Please read carefully: 
 1. Write a cover letter addressing:
 Why are you the best Organic Social Specialist for this role? Give us examples of accounts, campaigns, or content you’ve worked on — and include results where possible.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What’s the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?
 What are the last three books you’ve read?
 What do you do for fun?
 2. Explain what you’re doing now for a job:
 If you don’t have one, explain why.
 If you have one, explain why you’re looking elsewhere.
 3. Show us what you’ve done.

 And tell us what you actually did. 
 If something performed particularly well, even better. Give us the numbers.
 4. Upload your cover letter and resume.
 Ensure your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 Yes, our hiring process is challenging, but it’s our way of selecting the best — and your way of ensuring your AlgaeCal teammates are tops.
 Click the “Apply Now” button on this page and upload your cover letter and resume. 
 Note: Please include your cover letter WITH your resume in one document. Applications without a cover letter will not be read!

Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure.

 - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs.

 - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints.

 - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet.

 - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run.

 - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention.

 - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply.

 - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE).

 - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is.

 - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load.

 - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++.

 - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.

 - Slurm or other HPC schedulers.

 - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable.

 - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production.

 - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

You will work closely with customers and Jabil’s extended cross-functional teams (design, test, manufacturing, PMO, Quality) to deliver design and manufacturing test solutions.

Work closely with test equipment vendors as well as with test hardware developers on defining, designing, developing and optimizing test hardware solutions.

About Gusto 
 At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.
 All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .
 AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.
 About the Role: 
 Gusto is looking for a VC & PE Partnerships Manager to own and scale our relationships across venture capital (VC) and private equity (PE) firms.
 This role sits at the intersection of partnerships, investing, and go-to-market strategy. You’ll own how Gusto engages with the investor ecosystem in a way that is thoughtful, scalable, and aligned with long-term business priorities, and you’ll be accountable for the results of that motion across the function. Rather than managing a broad set of one-off relationships, this role focuses on building high-leverage, programmatic ecosystem partnerships that consistently show up early in a founder’s journey.
 You’ll partner closely with teams across various Partnerships teams, Marketing, Events, and Sales to define the right portfolio, engagement model, and success metrics for this motion.
 About the Team: 
 The Channel Partnerships function sits within Gusto’s broader Partnerships organization. We work cross-functionally to extend Gusto’s reach through trusted partners, while ensuring our motions scale sustainably over time. This team acts as a connective layer between the startup ecosystem and Gusto’s go-to-market engine—balancing long-term relationship building with clear ownership, guardrails, and outcomes.
 Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day: 
 Own Gusto’s VC & PE partnership strategy end to end, accountable for results across the function
 Define and maintain a clear partner portfolio, including which partners warrant 1:1 investment versus scaled engagement
 Build repeatable, programmatic partnership motions (e.g., portfolio company programs, founder and operator education, marketplace or platform integrations)
 Serve as the Tier 1 point of contact for a core group of high-impact ecosystem partners
 Collaborate closely with Partner Marketing and Events to design scalable programs and moments of engagement
 Partner with Recruit and other internal teams to align on net-new partner sourcing over time
 Track and evaluate ecosystem impact across metrics such as ARR, pipeline influence, and founder reach
 Represent Gusto externally as a credible, recognized voice in the VC & PE ecosystem, and provide thought leadership to internal teams and external partners
 Here’s what we're looking for: 
 5+ years of experience in partnerships, ecosystem development, venture or growth programs, or adjacent roles, with a track record of function-level impact
 3+ years of experience with the venture capital and private equity ecosystem , including founders, operators, and investors
 Proven ability to independently lead complex, cross-functional partnership initiatives that balance relationship depth with scalability
 Strong judgment around where to invest time and where to say “not now”
 Comfort working cross-functionally and influencing without direct authority
 Ability to translate ambiguous inputs into clear strategy and execution plans
 Experience working at or closely with a VC or PE firm, high-growth company, or ecosystem platform
 Background in program design, portfolio engagement, or platform partnerships
 Experience evaluating partnership impact beyond direct revenue attribution
 Our cash compensation amount for this role is $153,000 to $195,000 USD for Denver, Phoenix, Atlanta metro areas and $180,815 to $230,000 USD for San Francisco & New York and $146,940-$185,000 CAD for Toronto. Who We Are   
 Rising Edge Group is an electrical contracting company founded in 2002, specialization in high-voltage electrical solutions that power critical infrastructure across North America. With operations in both Canada and the United States, we partner with clients across the electrical utilities, renewable energy, and industrial sectors to design, build, and maintain the critical infrastructure systems communities and industries rely on.   
 Driven by a clear vision to strengthen the stability, reliability, and advancement of energy infrastructure, we take pride in delivering work that matters. Guided by our STRIDE values - Safety, Teamwork, Responsibility, Integrity, Deliver, and Excellence - we foster a people focused culture of growth, mentorship and collaboration where safety always come first.  
 What You'll Do   
 The Lead Project Controller serves as a senior technical resource within the Project Controls function, promoting the consistent application of project controls practices and providing guidance on complex or non-routine matters. The position supports Project Controllers in cost control, forecasting, earned value, cash flow, scheduling, risk and change management, and reporting. The role does not include direct supervisory or people-management responsibilities.
 To maintain sufficient capacity for technical leadership, complex project support, and participation in major estimates, the Lead Project Controller will typically carry a reduced portfolio equivalent to 30–50% of a standard Project Controller workload. This will generally include up to two Project Manager assignments and may be reduced further as technical support or estimating demands increase. Where practical, a limited portfolio will be retained to maintain a direct connection to project execution.
 As Rising Edge continues to expand, the Lead Project Controller will contribute to the development of practical, scalable Project Controls standards, tools, and processes. The successful candidate will be motivated by the opportunity to help shape a growing function and will be comfortable working in an environment where established processes continue to evolve. The role requires sound judgment and initiative to develop solutions that can support the organization as it scales.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Technical Leadership and Support 
 Serve as the senior technical resource for Project Controllers, Junior Project Controllers, and Project Assistants on complex Project Controls matters.
 Support complex forecasting, earned value, cash flow, scheduling, cost-control, change-management, and reporting issues.
 Review or advise on high-risk and technically complex deliverables, and help troubleshoot unusual project, contract, system, or reporting conditions.
 Coach team members through complex work while the assigned Project Controller retains ownership of routine project deliverables.
 Identify recurring technical gaps and convert them into practical standards, examples, training content, or process improvements.
 Escalate material technical or Project Controls risks to the Supervisor or Manager. The role provides technical guidance but does not assign work, manage performance, or hold administrative authority.
 Cost Control Forecasting and Performance Measurement 
 Provide advanced cost-control support across budgets, actual costs, commitments, accruals, estimate to complete, estimate at completion, and forecast trends.
 Lead or support complex monthly forecast and earned-value reviews, including coordination of inputs, validation of assumptions, and clear explanation of forecast movement.
 Challenge unsupported forecast assumptions and reconcile financial results with current scope, progress, schedule, procurement, and known project risks.
 Analyze material variances and identify the underlying cost drivers, exposure, opportunities, and required corrective actions.
 Support cash-flow modelling and time-phased cost analysis so financial forecasts reflect the expected sequence of project execution.
 Prepare or review concise, defensible reporting for Project Managers and senior leadership, and present technical findings when required.
 Estimating and Preconstruction Support 
 Act as the primary Project Controls contact for the Estimating team on major pursuits identified by the Manager.
 Support development of estimate-stage risk and opportunity registers, preliminary cash flows, execution schedules, contingency assumptions, reporting requirements, and Project Controls staffing plans.
 Challenge schedule, risk, cash-flow, cost, and execution assumptions before submission and identify gaps that may affect project delivery.
 Estimate to Execution Handover 
 Help establish the project control structure before award, including the work breakdown structure, cost and reporting framework, forecast approach, and initial control requirements.
 Participate in the estimate-to-execution handover for awarded projects and ensure key assumptions, risks, opportunities, cash flows, schedules, and contingency considerations are transferred clearly.
 Support the project team in reconciling the awarded estimate with the executed contract, baseline, procurement plan, initial forecast, and reporting requirements.
 Project Controls Standards Systems and Continuous Improvement

ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Customer Activation Manager at Ramp, you’ll help partner-sourced customers improve how they manage their finances. You’ll own a book of approximately 80 customers, guiding them through implementation and helping their teams adopt new workflows, including Ramp’s AI and agentic finance capabilities.

This role goes beyond getting customers live. You’ll work with finance leaders, their teams, and external partners to understand what needs to change, address resistance, and make sure customers see measurable value from Ramp. We’re looking for someone who’s led customers through change, is comfortable working with CFOs and Controllers, and uses AI regularly in their own work.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Guide partner-sourced customers from implementation through ongoing workflow adoption, with accountability for time to value and business outcomes.

 - Build a change management plan for each account: identify stakeholders, understand what’s slowing adoption, and help customer teams work through it.

 - Help CFOs and Controllers measure Ramp’s impact, including improvements in close cycles, spend visibility, variance reduction, and ROI.

 - Manage relationships across the customer’s organization, including finance leadership relationships you’ll own independently.

 - Use AI to prepare for calls, build customer materials, synthesize data, spot account risks, and reduce repetitive work.

 - Help customers evaluate and adopt Ramp’s agentic finance capabilities, including the changes these workflows require in their teams’ day-to-day work.

 - Work with Channel Partner Managers, Partner Consulting, Account Executives, and Technical Consulting to coordinate implementations and identify opportunities to expand Ramp’s use.

 - Share recurring customer needs, product gaps, and feedback with Product.

 - 5+ years in customer success, consulting, implementations, or a similar customer-facing role, with a consistent record of delivering customer outcomes and exceeding goals.

 - Experience driving workflow adoption and managing organizational change, including navigating stakeholder resistance. Finance or fintech experience is helpful but not required.

 - Regular, hands-on use of AI to prepare for calls, synthesize information, create customer-facing materials, and automate repetitive tasks.

 - The ability to build a business case for workflow changes and explain their financial impact to CFOs and Controllers, connecting implementation progress to business results.

 - Enough technical depth to work with Product and Engineering on integrations, APIs, and workflow design, and explain those topics to customers.

 - Success in a fast-paced GTM environment, ideally at a SaaS or fintech company.

 - Strong collaboration skills and the ability to get work done across Sales, Product, Operations, and other GTM teams.

 - Familiarity with FP&A, accounting platforms such as NetSuite, Sage, QuickBooks, or Xero, expense management, or other finance workflows.

 - Measurable results in expansion, retention, or time to value.

 - Experience at a company where AI was central to the product or how the team worked.

 - Experience managing 50+ customers at once, prioritizing across accounts, and turning open-ended problems into clear plans.

 - Experience working with third-party partners or consultants on customer activation and new use cases.

About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





Why we want you

 About Stripe
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

 As a platform company powering businesses all over the world, Stripe processes payments, runs marketplaces, detects fraud, helps entrepreneurs start internet businesses from anywhere in the world, builds world-class developer-friendly APIs, and more. The engineering teams at Stripe work on the business logic for all of that. As a software engineering manager at Stripe, you'll lead teams that build and expand APIs, services, and experiences. You'll also work with partners to launch new markets and vertical capabilities.
 Stripe Terminal helps our users extend their online presence to the physical world. The mission of the Terminal team is to make it as easy for businesses to accept in-person payments as the Stripe API has done for online payments—building for Unified Commerce. With Terminal, businesses can unify their in-person and online experiences, unlocking payments use cases that are right for their business model—whether it's creating a modern retail experience, extending their website to a pop-up store, or enabling a mobile point-of-sale at their next event.
 Within Terminal, the Commerce team focuses on the following to help make Unified Commerce a reality for businesses across the globe.
 Enterprise features—on-reader forms, tipping, gift cards

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



Device Infrastructure Services owns the full lifecycle of hardware and operating systems across 1Password. The team is looking for the Staff Engineer who will lead its next chapter: a deliberate shift from legacy device management patterns towards devops and AI-enabled operations.



You'll be the technical leader of this team, responsible for setting the roadmap for this transformation and making sure it gets executed. This isn't a role where you hand off a roadmap and step back: you'll be in the build alongside the team, coaching engineers and raising the ceiling on what they're capable of. If you're excited by building scalable systems, shaping the strategy behind tools the whole company depends on, and bringing out the best work in the people around you, we want to hear from you.





How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.



What we're looking for:

 - 7+ years of IT and enterprise endpoint management experience, including 2+ years at a senior or staff IC level, with a track record of building and managing endpoints with Gitops practices.

 - Demonstrate broad knowledge of enterprise endpoint management, deep operating system-level experience, and the ability to recognize patterns across a fleet and build fixes that prevent recurrence.

 - Practical experience using AI tools to enable or accelerate IT operations and the judgment to know where AI speeds things up versus where it introduces risk.

 - Proven ability to define and drive technical roadmaps, seeing around corners and balancing long-term vision with near-term execution.

 -  Strong scripting and IaC ability (Bash, Python, and Terraform at minimum) — both writing production-quality automation yourself and reviewing others' code with a critical eye.

 -  Deep working knowledge of enterprise security fundamentals as they apply to endpoints: encryption, patch/vulnerability management, EDR, least-privilege enforcement, and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar).

 - Lead through change, collaborate effectively, and mentor engineers while maintaining a focused and impactful team environment.





What you can expect:

 - Own the technical direction of our Device Infrastructure Services, the tooling and standards that keep ~2,000 endpoints compliant, configured, and secure.

 - Drive the technical direction of a DevOps operating model for the fleet — config-as-code, version control, code review, and CI/CD pipelines in place of manual console changes — and drive adoption of that model across the IT team.

 -  Lead the adoption of responsible agentic AI across the device team, building the guardrails that decide what agents can act on autonomously and what still needs a human checkpoint.

 -  Act as the final escalation point for high-severity endpoint incidents, including deep machine-level diagnosis on both macOS and Windows hardware.

 - Partner across IT, Security, and product teams building custom solutions and helping push their initiatives across the finish line.

 - Assess and pilot new tooling (e.g., MDM platform migrations, patch management systems) and drive build-vs-buy decisions.

 - Collaborate with product teams to advise on features from the perspective of a real-world enterprise device deployment, and lead Customer Zero initiatives — piloting and stress-testing our own product against our internal fleet before it reaches customers.



What success looks like:

 - Establishing a clear 12-month roadmap for the transition to a GitOps-based operating model.

 - Building device health metrics and remediation standards for machine security, performance, and employee experience.

 - Developing our AI-assisted operations strategy, with automation milestones that balance speed, human review, security and agentic workflows.

 - Supporting the unpredictable release cadence of major OS vendors, and making sure those updates land safely across the org.

 - Bringing the team along with you — at 1Password, we Put People First. This role isn't just about leveling up what we can do technically, it's also about coaching the team along the way.
